title: Nonprofits report heavy application and reporting effort and late payments on government contracts and grants

history.reason: Signal from Urban Institute national survey; data are from 2012.
Review correction: replaced misattributed 2009 human-service percentages with 2013-survey Figure 11 results; corrected Table 3 denominator.

provenance.session: session_01LQxkVvFKqYivoTtCXoQ4cs; reviewed corrections by Codex fix_merge_30_31

description: In the Urban Institute’s 2013 survey covering 2012, about 71 percent of responding government-funded nonprofits rated application complexity as a big or small problem; about 71 percent did so for reporting complexity and about 45 percent for late payments. Missing/not-applicable responses were excluded in Figure 11.
customer_segment: Charitable nonprofits with $100,000 or more in expenses and government contracts or grants; the smallest nonprofits are excluded from the survey frame.
context: Historical evidence about 2012 from the 2013 national survey; current prevalence and costs remain unverified. Earlier 75%/53% figures elsewhere in the same report concern 2009 human-service nonprofits and are not used as 2012 estimates.

evidence.text: Figure 11 (printed p. 25) reports application complexity as a big problem for 32% and a small problem for 39%; reporting complexity is 31% big and 40% small. Each totals about 71%, subject to rounding and exclusion of missing/not-applicable responses.
Figure 11 reports late payments beyond contract specifications as a big problem for 19% and a small problem for 26%, about 45% combined, excluding missing/not-applicable responses.

In the 2013-survey analysis of late payments (printed p. 32), nonprofits reporting late-payment problems were significantly more likely to draw on reserves, increase lines of credit, reduce programs, and close offices/sites; this association is not a causal estimate.
Grant-and-contract administration software or services could reduce this effort for small nonprofits.

alternatives: Grant-management software, accounting systems, consultants: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: Table 3 (printed p. 10) shows that nonprofits in the $100,000–$249,999 budget category comprise 17% of government-funded nonprofits in the survey distribution. It does not establish that 17% of all nonprofits in that size band receive government funding; surrounding prose is ambiguous on this denominator.

The evidence concerns 2012, not current practices. Figure 11 also shows 28%/29% reporting application/reporting complexity as not a problem and 55% reporting late payments as not a problem; missing/not-applicable answers were excluded.

uncertainty: Unknown: current prevalence, dollar cost of the effort, who buys tools, willingness to pay, and existing product coverage. Government-funding incidence within the smallest included budget band is not established by Table 3.
open_questions: Do newer data (for example nonprofit sector surveys since 2020) show the same pattern?
Which payers and program types cause most delays?
next_actions: Find a post-2020 primary source on nonprofit government payment timeliness and reporting burden.
